sections.heading: Polynomial division and the remainder theorem

questions.q: Find the remainder when $f(x)=x^3-2x^2+x-5$ is divided by $(x-2)$, using the remainder theorem.
questions.answer: By the remainder theorem, the remainder equals $f(2)$: $f(2)=8-8+2-5=-3$.

questions.q: Two functions are given: $f(x)=x^3$ and $g(x)=2^x$. Explain which function eventually grows faster as $x$ increases, and estimate the crossover point using the values $f(10)=1000$, $g(10)=1024$, $f(8)=512$, $g(8)=256$.
questions.answer: Exponential functions eventually always outgrow polynomial functions as $x\to\infty$, regardless of the polynomial's degree, because the exponential's rate of increase itself keeps growing while the polynomial's relative rate of increase slows. Comparing the given values: at $x=8$, $f(8)=512>g(8)=256$ (polynomial ahead), but by $x=10$, $g(10)=1024>f(10)=1000$ (exponential has overtaken it) — so the crossover happens between $x=8$ and $x=10$.

questions.q: An investment of 5000 dollars grows according to $A(t)=5000(1.06)^t$, where $t$ is the number of years. Find the value of the investment after 5 years, to the nearest dollar, and state the annual growth rate as a percentage.
questions.answer: $A(5)=5000(1.06)^5=5000(1.3382)\approx6691$ dollars. The annual growth rate is $6\%$, since the growth factor is $1.06=1+0.06$.

sections.heading: Applying the zero product property to polynomial equations

questions.q: Solve $x^3-5x^2+6x=0$ by factoring completely and applying the zero product property.
questions.answer: Factor out $x$: $x(x^2-5x+6)=0$, then factor the quadratic: $x(x-2)(x-3)=0$. By the zero product property, $x=0$, $x=2$, or $x=3$.

questions.q: Two savings accounts grow according to $A(t)=1000(1.03)^t$ and $B(t)=1000(1.05)^t$. Explain which account grows faster, and find the difference in value after 10 years, to the nearest dollar.
questions.answer: Account $B$ grows faster because it has a larger growth factor ($1.05>1.03$, meaning a higher annual interest rate). After 10 years: $A(10)=1000(1.03)^{10}\approx1344$, $B(10)=1000(1.05)^{10}\approx1629$. Difference: $1629-1344=285$ dollars.

Find the remainder when $f(x)=x^3+5x^2+2x+3$ is divided by $(x-(-2))$, using the remainder theorem.
questions.answer: By the remainder theorem, the remainder equals $f(-2)$: $f(-2)=(-2)^3+(5)(-2)^2+(2)(-2)+(3)=11$.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $f(x)=x^3-6x^2-7x-15$ is divided by $(x-(2))$, using the remainder theorem.
questions.answer: By the remainder theorem, the remainder equals $f(2)$: $f(2)=(2)^3+(-6)(2)^2+(-7)(2)+(-15)=-45$.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $f(x)=x^3+3x^2+9$ is divided by $(x-(-4))$, using the remainder theorem.
questions.answer: By the remainder theorem, the remainder equals $f(-4)$: $f(-4)=(-4)^3+(3)(-4)^2+(0)(-4)+(9)=-7$.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $f(x)=x^3+3x^2+6x+14$ is divided by $(x-(-1))$, using the remainder theorem.
questions.answer: By the remainder theorem, the remainder equals $f(-1)$: $f(-1)=(-1)^3+(3)(-1)^2+(6)(-1)+(14)=10$.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $f(x)=x^3-4x^2-4x-15$ is divided by $(x-(-1))$, using the remainder theorem.
questions.answer: By the remainder theorem, the remainder equals $f(-1)$: $f(-1)=(-1)^3+(-4)(-1)^2+(-4)(-1)+(-15)=-16$.

Solve $x^3+3x^2-10x=0$ by factoring completely. Excluding the solution $x=0$, find the other two solutions as an ordered pair (smaller first).
questions.answer: Factor out $x$: $x(x^2+3x-10)=0$, then factor the quadratic: $x(x-(-5))(x-(2))=0$. By the zero product property, $x=0$, $x=-5$, or $x=2$. Excluding $0$: $\left(-5,2\right)$.

questions.q: Solve $x^3+11x^2+18x=0$ by factoring completely. Excluding the solution $x=0$, find the other two solutions as an ordered pair (smaller first).
questions.answer: Factor out $x$: $x(x^2+11x+18)=0$, then factor the quadratic: $x(x-(-9))(x-(-2))=0$. By the zero product property, $x=0$, $x=-9$, or $x=-2$. Excluding $0$: $\left(-9,-2\right)$.

questions.q: Solve $x^3+3x^2-40x=0$ by factoring completely. Excluding the solution $x=0$, find the other two solutions as an ordered pair (smaller first).
questions.answer: Factor out $x$: $x(x^2+3x-40)=0$, then factor the quadratic: $x(x-(-8))(x-(5))=0$. By the zero product property, $x=0$, $x=-8$, or $x=5$. Excluding $0$: $\left(-8,5\right)$.

questions.q: Solve $x^3+7x^2-18x=0$ by factoring completely. Excluding the solution $x=0$, find the other two solutions as an ordered pair (smaller first).
questions.answer: Factor out $x$: $x(x^2+7x-18)=0$, then factor the quadratic: $x(x-(2))(x-(-9))=0$. By the zero product property, $x=0$, $x=2$, or $x=-9$. Excluding $0$: $\left(-9,2\right)$.

questions.q: Solve $x^3-15x^2+56x=0$ by factoring completely. Excluding the solution $x=0$, find the other two solutions as an ordered pair (smaller first).
questions.answer: Factor out $x$: $x(x^2-15x+56)=0$, then factor the quadratic: $x(x-(7))(x-(8))=0$. By the zero product property, $x=0$, $x=7$, or $x=8$. Excluding $0$: $\left(7,8\right)$.
